transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because things got out of hand at work. I'm in HR, and we had this new onboarding program we were working on. I just... I pushed ahead with the launch. I committed company money and booked vendor time before any of the official approvals were in place. At the time, it just felt bold and necessary, like I was getting things done. But now... well, now I'm on administrative leave and everyone is asking what I was thinking. So, my job sent me here.
In the days or weeks leading up to this, did you notice your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep?

Yeah, actually. For the past few weeks, I've felt... well, either brilliantly alive, like I could finally show leadership what HR can really be, or just suddenly furious. If someone questioned me on something—even over small edits or routine budget questions—I would get incredibly angry. It was very intense.
How long has this period of feeling unusually energetic, elated, or irritable lasted—days, or has it been going on for a week or more?
Definitely more than a week. I'd say... this has really been building for about a month. It started right around the time the new executive came in and started challenging my onboarding redesign.
Over the past month, have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or stimulant medications more than usual?

No, not at all. I mean... I drink occasionally, but nothing out of the ordinary lately. And I definitely haven't been using any drugs or, you know, stimulants or anything like that. It wasn't fueled by anything I was taking.

During this past month, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things others didn't, or holding beliefs—like having special powers or a special mission—that others found unusual or hard to believe?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen things that weren't there. And I didn't think I had any... special powers or anything. I just felt like I had a really clear vision for my department, but it wasn't anything supernatural or strange like that. Just... very confident in my work.

Before this past month, have you ever had another period—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or on the flip side, a period of deep depression, low energy, or loss of interest in things?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good or had a lot of energy, but nothing like this past month. And as for depression... no, I haven't really had any periods where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in everything. This whole experience recently is pretty new for me.
During this past month, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual—for example, feeling fully rested after only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I usually get about seven or eight hours a night, and that's been pretty consistent. I haven't had any nights where I only slept a few hours and felt fine the next day, or anything like that. I just sleep normally.
During this past month, have you noticed your thoughts racing or jumping quickly from one idea to another, faster than usual?

No, not really. My thoughts have been pretty steady. I mean, I've had a lot of ideas for work, like I said, but they weren't racing or jumping all over the place. I could focus on them just fine. It didn't feel out of control or faster than normal.

Besides this work situation, have you noticed yourself engaging in other impulsive or risky behaviors this past month—like unusual spending, big purchases, or other decisions that felt out of character for you?

No, I haven't done anything like that. My spending has been completely normal. I haven't, you know, made any huge purchases or taken any weird risks. It really is just the work situation we talked about... outside of that, everything else in my life has been pretty much business as usual.
During this past month, have you noticed yourself talking a lot more than usual, or feeling like you just can't stop talking or that people have trouble keeping up with you?

Yeah, actually, I have noticed that. Especially at work. In meetings, I can hear myself talking a lot faster and, well, longer than I usually do. I'll jump straight from employee engagement to gallery layouts, and then right into retention metrics. It gets to the point where people practically have to raise their hands just to stop me and get a word in. So, yes, I guess I definitely have been talking a lot more than normal.
Does anyone in your immediate family—parents, siblings, or children—have a history of depression, bipolar disorder, or similar mood episodes?
No, not that I know of. My parents never mentioned anything like that, and my brother seems fine. As far as I'm aware, there's no history of any mood issues or depression in my family.
